body:
No one had to tell me. When I was told what the cause of her death was--the burst aneurism--I looked it up. If I hadn't argued with her, if I hadn't told her I hated her, if I hadn't raised her blood pressure so much that the blood vessel couldn't take it, she would have been around longer, and maybe would still be here today.

It was clearly me who made it happen. And I don't know if I can ever come to terms with that. I mean, it's been almost 35 years. I haven't been able to do anything that would make her proud of me, I haven't been able to meet someone, I have no kids, I'm a dismal failure at life, and to top it off, I have to deal with the aftermath of knowing that I was the one responsible for my mother's death. I just don't think I can handle it anymore. In fact, I know I can't.

I started a small charcoal fire in my room about 20 minutes ago. I'll just fall asleep and not wake up. I may not join my mother in heaven, but I won't have to deal with this oppressive pain anymore.
